findings.title: Budget unit math assumes a 2-decimal currency (CENTS_TO_MICROS = 10_000); no currency on BudgetDelta
findings.description: Meta budgets are integers in the account currency's minor unit; for zero-decimal currencies (JPY, KRW, TWD, HUF, etc.) the integer is the whole unit. The constant conversion misstates such budgets 100x to the policy engine and preview, and the bridge's micros->cents conversion would set a 100x budget. Impact on zero-decimal currencies is INFERRED from Marketing API semantics; no effect for SAR/USD/EUR.
findings.recommendation: Fetch account currency with the budget lookup, apply a per-currency exponent table, set BudgetDelta.currency, reject unknown currencies.

findings.title: Google reports silently truncated and labelled complete
evidence: node scratch trunc.mjs => exit 0: rows=100 truncated=undefined core truncated=false
findings.description: Provider slices each account's rows to exactly `limit` and never sets Report.truncated; core detects truncation only when rows > limit, so accounts with more entities than `limit` (default 100) produce totals missing entities while summary.complete is true. No ORDER BY, so dropped rows are arbitrary.
findings.recommendation: Fetch limit+1 or track overflow and set truncated:true; add ORDER BY metrics.cost_micros DESC; add an overflow test.

findings.title: protected_accounts bypassable for Google via dashed / customers/ id formats
findings.description: PolicyEngine compares the raw op.accountId string against protected_accounts; the Google provider later normalizes '123-456-7890' and 'customers/1234567890' to '1234567890', so a protected account is writable when addressed in the format Google's UI displays. Cloud allow-scope normalizes dashes, but the protection rail does not.
findings.recommendation: Canonicalize account ids per provider before checkStaticPolicy; add a dashed-id test.

findings.title: Budget rails are currency-blind; new budgets uncapped by default
findings.description: Pct cap applies only when fromMicros exists; google_create_campaign and google_api_create campaignBudgets have no 'from', and max_daily_budget_micros defaults to null, so new budgets are unbounded (then enabled by a separate, budget-unchecked status call). The absolute cap is one micros number applied to USD/SAR/EGP alike; BudgetDelta.currency and ReportRow.currency are never set by the Google provider.
findings.recommendation: Set currency from customer.currency_code on deltas/rows; per-currency caps; default absolute cap for new budgets; cumulative per-session drift cap.

findings.title: Tool descriptions/comments promise always-paused creation that only policy delivers
findings.description: google_api_create description says campaign status is forced to PAUSED and the RSA planner comment says RSAs always start paused, but both are conditional on guard.forcePausedCreation; with paused_creation:false, live spending objects are created while the model is told they are paused.

findings.title: Engine marks all live Google rows complete and takes currency from config

The fixture provider models lag; the live path cannot.
findings.recommendation: Derive per-platform completeness (Google conversion lag) and read customer.currency_code/time_zone on first use.

findings.title: google_create_campaign accepts PMax/Shopping/Video/Display but builds a Search-shaped manual-CPC campaign with default networks

findings.recommendation: Fetch customer.time_zone in listAccounts and resolve presets per account.

findings.recommendation: Surface the probe error or mark manager accounts so they are excluded.

findings.title: reddit_set_budget allows silent LIFETIME_SPEND -> DAILY_SPEND re-typing at the same amount; rails see 0% delta and preview omits the type switch
findings.description: The preview prints the campaign's current goal_type and old->new goal_value but never the requested budget_type; budgetDeltas compares raw micros regardless of type. A lifetime CBO budget of 3,000 units re-sent as DAILY_SPEND 3,000 shows '~ campaign X LIFETIME_SPEND 3000000000 -> 3000000000' (0% delta, passes max_budget_delta_pct; max_daily_budget_micros defaults to null) and on apply PATCHes goal_type to DAILY_SPEND, i.e. the whole flight budget every day. The engine bridge hard-codes budget_type DAILY_SPEND, so any proposal against a lifetime-budgeted Reddit CBO campaign takes this path with an uninformed approval.
findings.recommendation: Reject or separately gate goal_type changes in reddit_set_budget; print old->new goal_type as a change/coercion line; normalize lifetime vs daily before computing the percent delta.

findings.title: reconciled=yes is tautological without provider totals
findings.description: The only unconditional reconciliation check (entity_rows_sum_to_platform_spend) compares a sum of per-entity aggregates to the platform aggregate over the same rows, so it is mathematically identical and always passes. Provider-based checks run only when the provider returned non-empty totals (reads.py:266 defaults to {}). Thus reconciled=True can mean no external corroboration occurred.
findings.recommendation: Make reconciliation tri-state (reconciled / not_reconciled / no_external_oracle) or require at least one provider-sourced check before reconciled can be true.

findings.title: Ratios blend full spend with partial conversion data (CPA overstated, ROAS understated)
evidence: probe.py PROBE1 => spend=700 conversions=10 cpa=70.00 roas=1.428571 (converting days alone give CPA 20 / ROAS 5)
findings.description: Within an entity/window, spend is summed over all rows but conversions/conversion_value only over rows that reported them. When some days lack conversions, CPA = full_spend/partial_conversions and ROAS = partial_value/full_spend, a large distortion. The MISSING_METRIC flag is attached but the misleading ratio is still emitted as an authoritative number.
findings.recommendation: When a ratio's numerator is missing on rows that still contribute spend to the denominator (or vice versa), suppress the ratio or compute it over the subset where both sides are present and label the basis.

findings.title: current_window.is_complete mislabeled incomplete when only the previous window had incomplete rows
evidence: probe2.py => current_window.is_complete=False despite all current rows complete
findings.description: platform_flags unions INCOMPLETE_WINDOW from both current and previous entity rows; current_complete additionally requires INCOMPLETE_WINDOW not in platform_flags, while previous_complete omits that guard. A fully-complete current window is labeled incomplete because the previous window had an incomplete row.
findings.recommendation: Derive each window's completeness only from its own rows; do not gate current_complete on the shared platform_flags set.

findings.title: Provider reconciliation fails spuriously when the read covered rows outside current-union-previous
evidence: probe.py PROBE3 => rows_reconcile_to_provider_spend False (provider 1109 vs rows 110)
findings.description: provider_totals is the provider total for the entire read window, but reconciliation sums only rows inside the two comparison windows. Any buffer/gap day makes the spend and row-count checks fail even though the data is correct.
findings.recommendation: Reconcile the provider total against rows over the exact window the total covers, or store per-window provider totals.

findings.title: Two divergent measurement engines (Python Decimal vs TS float) with different null semantics
findings.description: The engine computes metrics with exact Decimal and any-row-present summation; the platform core computes the same cross-platform report with JS floating-point numbers and all-rows-required null rules, and reconstructs ROAS via float spend*roas. The same account/window can yield different numbers and different null outcomes depending on which subsystem renders it.
findings.recommendation: Define one canonical metric contract (precision, rounding, null policy) enforced by both engines or route authoritative numbers through one engine; add cross-engine golden tests.

findings.title: Reconciliation covers only spend and row_count; ROAS/CPA numerators never reconciled
findings.description: Only provider spend and row_count are reconciled; conversions and conversion_value (the drivers of ROAS/CPA) are never cross-checked against provider totals, so reconciled=yes says nothing about conversion correctness.
findings.recommendation: Add provider reconciliation for conversions and conversion_value and down-rank reconciled when they are unavailable.

findings.title: Cross-platform total combines windows with equal dates but possibly different timezones
findings.description: compare_periods requires identical (start,end) across platforms but ignores timezone, and _combine discards timezone, so two platforms in different timezones with the same date labels are combined despite different real day boundaries.
findings.recommendation: Require matching timezones to combine, or attach a TIMEZONE_MISMATCH note to the cross-platform total.

findings.title: Daily day-over-day change compares nearest present days, not calendar-adjacent days
findings.description: The daily series iterates over sorted present days; previous is the prior present element regardless of calendar gaps, so a missing day makes two non-adjacent days appear day-over-day and can trip the +/-50% flag.
findings.recommendation: Compute change against the calendar-previous day and emit null/a gap marker when it is absent.

findings.title: pacing uses active-day average, can read as over-budget for intermittent entities
findings.description: average_daily = spend/active_days and pacing = average_daily/budget, so an entity running few days can be flagged over_budget on its active-day burst even when its window-average is well under budget; the per-active-day basis is not surfaced.
findings.recommendation: Surface the active-day basis explicitly or offer both active-day and window-day pacing.

findings.title: Reconciliation uses exact Decimal equality after per-row 6dp quantization
findings.description: Each row spend is quantized to 1e-6 then summed and compared with == to a single-quantized provider total; accumulated sub-micro rounding can produce rare spurious reconciliation failures.
findings.recommendation: Reconcile with a tolerance (e.g. within one currency minor unit) instead of exact equality.

key_findings: Ratio aggregation is correct everywhere (sum raw then divide, never average ratios); zero denominators return None and missing metrics stay None, all confirmed by tests and probes.
reconciled=yes is tautological when the provider supplies no totals: the only unconditional check compares the row sum to itself (P2, VERIFIED_RUNTIME).
CPA/ROAS silently blend full-window spend with partial conversion data when some days lack conversions, distorting the ratio ~3.5x in a probe while still printing an authoritative number (P2).

Two independent metric engines coexist: engine uses exact Decimal with any-row-present nulls, platform core uses JS float with all-rows-required nulls, so the same metric can differ across surfaces (P2).
current_window completeness is mislabeled incomplete when only the previous window had incomplete rows (asymmetric check, P3).
Provider spend/row-count reconciliation fails spuriously whenever the read window exceeds current-union-previous; conversions/value are never reconciled at all (P3).

findings.title: Direct X Ads / OpenAI Ads never set data_complete_through, so conversion lag is not surfaced and recent days count as complete
findings.description: ProviderResult.data_complete_through defaults to None and the X/OpenAI performance reads omit it. In normalize.py the INCOMPLETE_WINDOW flag is only added when a boundary exists and is_complete is True whenever the boundary is None, so every row from these providers is treated as settled. INCOMPLETE_WINDOW is the only conversion-lag/freshness signal and it drives the compute.py incomplete-window suppression, which these providers bypass.
findings.recommendation: Require every read provider to supply data_complete_through (or make its absence a loud PARTIAL_SOURCE/SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE rather than silent completeness); at minimum flag rows from providers with no completeness boundary.

findings.description: The report tool's currency-separation, spend-weighted ROAS, and null-on-missing claims are all honoured by report-summary.ts, but conversions is an additive metric summed across every row in a currency group (across providers/accounts sharing a currency) with no attribution disclosure, and the 'complete' flag passed in is !truncated && errors.length===0 (builtin.ts:138) i.e. nothing about data freshness or attribution maturity.

key_findings: ATTRIBUTION_DIFFERS flag is defined (common.py:64) but never emitted anywhere in engine/src or engine/tests; provider attribution strings are captured then dropped (dead capability).

Cross-platform conversion/ROAS totals sum conversions across providers with different attribution windows and are NOT suppressed or flagged (compute.py:310-326, _combine at :282), contradicting the compare_periods 'only when sources are compatible' claim.

findings.title: No statistical significance / sample-size engine exists; recommendations rest on raw deltas only
findings.description: The only analysis computed is arithmetic deltas and ratios. No variance, standard error, confidence interval, significance test, or minimum-detectable-effect anywhere, and no statistics library is a dependency. compare_periods returns relative percentages with no indication whether a move is distinguishable from noise.
findings.recommendation: Attach sample-size context (conversions, clicks) to every delta and compute a crude significance/CI band for rate metrics so the output itself signals when a difference is within noise.

findings.title: summarize_window flags day-over-day moves on relative change only, ignoring base size (fires on 2->3 conversions)
evidence: runtime: summarize_rows on 2->3->4 daily conversions => flagged_days ['2026-08-02'], flags ['conversions_moved_up']
findings.description: The day-anomaly flag is a pure relative-change threshold (DAY_CHANGE_FLAG=0.5) with no floor on the absolute base. A 2->3 conversion day (noise) is flagged identically to a material move; the skill explicitly says such a move is not a trend, but the tool emits the flag anyway and relies on the LLM prose to discard it.
findings.recommendation: Gate the flag on an absolute floor (suppress conversion flags below a minimum base) or carry the base alongside the flag so consumers can weight it.

findings.title: propose_change accepts a recommendation with no evidence linkage and an empty measurement plan
evidence: rg measurement_plan engine/src (passthrough only, no validation)
findings.description: A proposal carries no link to the data that justified it (no analysis artifact id, no sample size, no comparison window). reason/measurement_plan/reversal_plan are free-text; both plans default to empty and are never validated for presence or content, even for budget/status-flip changes. Nothing in the pipeline can tell whether a change is backed by sufficient data.
findings.recommendation: Require proposals to cite the analysis artifact they rest on, require a non-empty measurement plan for budget/status-flip operations, and surface underlying sample size on the approval card.

findings.title: classify_risk is blind to data basis; risk is operational only, never statistical
findings.description: Risk flags are derived solely from the operation name, schema, and before/after values (status_flip, budget_delta, destructive_change, policy_high_risk). No parameter carries performance data, conversions, or sample size. A budget cut driven by 36 conversions and one driven by 3,600 produce identical risk flags.
findings.recommendation: Add a data-basis dimension to the reviewer card (window length, conversions observed, whether the move exceeds normal variation) sourced from the cited analysis artifact.

findings.title: Statistical discipline exists only as prose guidance the model may ignore
findings.description: The only sample-size awareness is written instruction to the LLM. It is sound but unenforced: no tool refuses, caveats, or gates on it, and no eval tests it. Experiments (holdout/geo/lift) are things the agent may recommend in prose; none are implemented.
findings.recommendation: Add an eval that presents a thin/noisy window and asserts the agent withholds or heavily caveats a recommendation; back the prose with a deterministic small-base caveat in the tool output.

findings.title: Demo proposal path hard-codes a budget-cut recommendation with no sample-size check (fixture, reachable pattern)
findings.description: The scripted demo emits a canned budget-cut proposal never derived from the analysis artifact it produced; the decision is hardcoded. It is a legitimate deterministic demo (gated by scripted:demo model and with_proposal, cannot reach a real platform), but it encodes the intended product behavior: produce and execute a budget change from a two-week comparison of a campaign averaging ~3 conversions/day, with no significance step and only a 7-day (~21-conversion) measurement plan.
findings.recommendation: Keep as a demo but do not treat it as evidence that recommendations are statistically grounded; pair it with a demo/eval showing the agent declining on insufficient data.

key_findings: No statistical significance, sample-size, confidence-interval, or variance computation exists anywhere in engine or platform; no stats library (scipy/statsmodels/numpy) is even a dependency (VERIFIED_CODE).
compare_periods/compute.py emit only absolute and relative deltas, with no uncertainty signal and no base-size caveat; relative % on tiny bases looks identical to real trends.
summarize_window flags day-over-day moves on relative change >=50% with no absolute floor, so a 2->3 conversion day (noise) is flagged as an anomaly (VERIFIED_RUNTIME).
propose_change carries no evidence linkage (no analysis artifact id, no sample size) and measurement_plan/reversal_plan default to empty and are never validated, even for budget/status changes.
classify_risk assesses only operational risk of the mutation; it is blind to whether the decision is statistically justified.
Sample-size discipline lives solely as unenforced prose in instructions.md and the anomaly-and-significance skill; no code gate and no eval guards it.
Net: the AI can make and execute a confident recommendation on insufficient data, constrained only by LLM adherence to prose guidance.
B3.disagreements: anomaly-and-significance.md frames the missing significance engine as deliberate caution, but the code actively emits small-base noise as anomaly flags (VERIFIED_RUNTIME: 2->3 conversions flagged), pushing toward over-reaction and contradicting the doc's cautious spirit. instructions.md:16-17 lists confidence as something the agent explains, implying a confidence concept, but in code confidence is only a free-text prose field with no computation behind it. The AI media buyer framing implies data-grounded decisions, yet the propose/execute pipeline carries no evidence linkage or data-sufficiency check, so a recommendation on insufficient data is fully reachable.
B3.not_verified: Actual LLM behavior at inference on a thin window is NOT_VERIFIED: no model API was exercised (the demo uses a scripted model), so whether a real model obeys the prose guidance is unknown; I verified only that nothing in code forces it to. Did not exhaustively read every provider adapter in platform/packages/*, though the platform-wide statistical-term scan returned no relevant hits. Did not execute the full demo-with-proposal end to end (verified that path by reading; ran compute/summary unit tests and a direct summarize_rows invocation).

evidence: engine/src/paid_media_agent/tools/compute.py:49-68 (sum returns total when any value seen)
findings.description: A metric present on some rows and absent on others is summed over present rows only, with no flag for impressions/clicks. B8 probe: day-2 impressions missing -> aggregate.impressions=1000 (true 2000), ctr=0.20 (true 0.10), missing=(). The cross-platform total is not suppressed because the gap is impressions, not conversions.
findings.recommendation: Treat a metric present on a strict subset of in-window rows as MISSING_METRIC/PARTIAL_SOURCE; require per-metric day-coverage == window day-count before emitting a ratio; extend the flag to impressions/clicks.
findings.failure_scenario: Gapped provider coverage of impressions looks like a complete window; the model presents a doubled CTR as fact and recommends on it.

findings.title: Conversion-definition conflation within and across platforms (purchases/results/installs/checkouts summed as one metric)
findings.description: normalize treats conversions/purchases/results as one column (first present wins per row), so one platform read can mix three objective-dependent definitions; the cross-platform sum then combines Google all-conversions, Meta purchases, Apple installs and Pinterest checkouts into one conversions figure and derives portfolio CVR/CPA/ROAS. Nothing records which event each count represents.
findings.recommendation: Record conversion_source_key/conversion_kind on PerformanceRow; set MISSING_METRIC or a new MIXED_CONVERSION_DEFINITION flag when more than one key is used in one artifact; refuse or segment cross-platform aggregation across differing event kinds; drop 'results' from the purchase key list.
findings.failure_scenario: A portfolio CPA/ROAS treats app installs (no revenue) and purchases as the same conversion, dragging blended ROAS and driving a budget reallocation across non-comparable events.

findings.title: Two divergent measurement engines (Python Decimal vs TypeScript float) with different null semantics
evidence: platform/packages/core/src/report-summary.ts:19-38 (float number; total null unless every row has the metric; spend-weighted ROAS)
findings.description: The engine and the platform core each compute the same metrics with different numeric types (exact Decimal vs float), different null policies (any-row-present vs all-rows-required), and different ROAS reconstruction. The same account/window can produce different spend/ROAS/CPA depending on which subsystem rendered it; there is no cross-engine golden test.
findings.recommendation: Define one canonical metric contract (precision, rounding, null policy, ratio-basis rules) enforced by both engines, or route all authoritative numbers through one engine; add a cross-engine golden test.
findings.failure_scenario: A currency group where one row lacks conversion_value shows null on the platform card but a number in the engine report, or cents drift on large float sums; two surfaces disagree on the same KPI.

findings.title: No statistical significance/sample-size engine; small-base noise is emitted as a structured flag
findings.description: The only analysis is arithmetic deltas; there is no variance, CI, significance test or MDE, and no stats library is a dependency. The day-anomaly flag fires on relative change >=50% with no base floor, so a 2->3 conversion day is flagged conversions_moved_up. The structured flags/flagged_days the model consumes are polluted with small-base noise.
findings.recommendation: Attach sample-size context (conversions/clicks) to every delta; gate day flags on an absolute floor; compute a crude CI/Wilson/Poisson band on rate metrics so the tool output itself distinguishes signal from noise.
findings.failure_scenario: A campaign's conversions move 2->3; the structured flag marks it an anomaly; the model escalates to a budget recommendation on statistical noise.

findings.title: propose_change carries no evidence linkage or sample size and empty-defaulting plans; classify_risk is blind to data basis
evidence: engine/src/paid_media_agent/tools/writes.py:389-450 (propose reads current provider state only, no analysis artifact)
findings.description: A proposal has no link to the data justifying it: no analysis_artifact_id, no sample size, no comparison window; measurement and reversal plans default empty and are never validated even for budget/status-flip ops. The risk surface shown to the reviewer describes what the mutation does, not whether it is statistically justified; a change backed by 36 conversions and one backed by 3,600 produce identical risk flags.
findings.recommendation: Require proposals to cite the analysis artifact id, a non-empty measurement/reversal plan for budget/status-flip ops, and the observed sample size on the approval card; add a data-basis dimension to classify_risk.
findings.failure_scenario: The AI stages a budget cut justified by a single noisy day with a blank measurement plan; the system accepts it, the reviewer sees only operational risk, and after one approval it executes.

findings.title: Cloud overview sums spend/conversions/value across currencies and providers; ROAS tile is structurally 0x
findings.description: The Arabic-first overview reduces every row into one totals object with no currency/provider grouping; because conversion_value is never requested, totals.value is always 0 and the headline ROAS tile renders 0x whenever a provider is connected, while spend/conversions sum USD+SAR and Meta+Google purchases. The upstream summarizeReport does this correctly and is unused.
findings.recommendation: Request conversion_value (or reuse summarizeReport's currency groups and roas_method); render per-currency tile groups; caption conversions platform-attributed/not-deduplicated; add a test asserting the tile is non-zero for sandbox data.
findings.failure_scenario: A KSA merchant with a SAR Snapchat account and a USD Meta account sees one spend figure off by the FX ratio and a 0x ROAS, the first profitability number the product shows.

findings.title: Cloud read boundary discards the currency-safe summary and drops provider warnings
evidence: platform/apps/cloud/lib/cloud/reads.ts:53-58 (keeps only rows/truncated; warnings built from errors only)
findings.description: The core computes a currency-grouped summary with a complete flag and a currency-safety warning for exactly the unresolved-currency case; the cloud boundary keeps only rows and truncated, so the one safeguard is silently dropped before the UI, enabling client-side cross-currency sums with no caution.
findings.recommendation: Propagate summary (with complete and currency groups) and warnings through reads.ts and surface both; never expose raw rows for aggregation without the currency grouping.
findings.failure_scenario: A summary-endpoint consumer cross-currency sums rows whose currency could not be resolved, with no warning that the core had flagged them.

findings.title: Sandbox synthetic data runs the production PolicyEngine/audit path with no per-row synthetic marker, gated only by a deploy-wide flag
evidence: platform/apps/cloud/lib/markting/sandbox-provider.ts:99-143 (synthetic metrics, no quality flag, no synthetic marker on report rows)
platform/apps/cloud/lib/markting/runtime.ts:18-26 (swaps provider for every principal, same PolicyEngine/Postgres/audit)
findings.description: Demo data is routed through the production approvals/audit path. The guard is a global boolean, not per-tenant or per-environment, and report rows carry no field a consumer can key on to tell synthetic from real (markers exist only on the list tool and write result). If the flag ships to production or a staging DB is shared, all tenants see synthetic fully-complete data driving the assistant, with audit/approval records indistinguishable from real.
findings.recommendation: Gate demo mode per-organization, stamp every sandbox report row with synthetic:true/data_source, and assert at the write/apply boundary that synthetic providers cannot run under a non-demo organization.
findings.failure_scenario: MARKTING_DEMO_MODE=true reaches production; a real tenant's assistant analyses synthetic complete metrics and stages real-looking proposals in the shared audit store.

findings.title: Budget percentage-delta cap silently bypassed when prior budget is unknown; default policy has no absolute ceiling
evidence: platform/packages/google/src/provider.ts:430, x/src/writes.ts:24, reddit/src/provider.ts:298, tiktok/src/provider.ts:336 (creates push toMicros only)
findings.description: When fromMicros is absent (every create, and an Apple update whose readback lacked a budget) the percentage cap is skipped; the only remaining numeric guard is the absolute cap, which defaults to null. Under the shipped default, an operation without a known prior budget can be assigned an arbitrarily large daily budget and pass policy. Partially mitigated because paused_creation coerces new entities to PAUSED, but the budget is still written.
findings.recommendation: Require an explicit absolute cap (reject null in production) and treat an absent fromMicros as cannot-verify -> fail closed rather than skip the percentage check; re-check budget policy at apply().
findings.failure_scenario: A newly created campaign is assigned a very large daily budget, passes policy because fromMicros is absent and the abs cap is null, then a later status flip starts delivery at that budget.

findings.title: translate.ts ignores the declared unit on the proposal field (unvalidated engine<->bridge unit contract)
evidence: platform/apps/cloud/lib/markting/translate.ts:86-92,148-152 (reads after.value, multiplies by 1_000_000; unit never consulted)
findings.description: The bridge assumes the engine always emits daily_budget in whole account-currency units and always multiplies by 1e6. True for the current fixture catalog but unenforced; if a live engine read surfaced a budget in minor units or micros with unit:'cents'/'micros', translate would still multiply by 1e6, a 100x or 1,000,000x error. The declared unit is dropped.
findings.recommendation: Validate after.unit against an expected enum and convert explicitly; fail 'unsupported' on any unexpected unit.
findings.failure_scenario: A future engine read returns daily_budget in cents with unit:'cents'; the bridge multiplies by 1e6 instead of 1e4, writing a 100x budget.

findings.title: Providers coerce missing conversions to 0 (contra semantics doc); zero-conversion rule then proposes a pause
findings.description: Six providers emit 0 for absent conversions, violating the published missing!=zero rule; for Meta the 0 is a definition artefact (omni_purchase only). The zero-conversion-spend audit rule cannot distinguish a lead-gen/traffic campaign from broken tracking and attaches a pause action. Execution requires preview+approval, so not P0.
findings.recommendation: Return undefined when the mapped action is absent; for Meta select the conversion action from the campaign objective or expose it as a parameter; have the rule skip rows whose conversion metric is absent rather than zero.
findings.failure_scenario: A well-performing lead-gen Meta campaign reports conversions:0 because only omni_purchase is counted; the audit recommends pausing it as waste.

findings.title: Incrementality guardrail (platform-attributed != incremental) is prompt-only on the live path
evidence: engine/instructions.md:20 (do not imply platform attribution is incremental)
findings.description: The distinction between platform-attributed and incremental lift is enforced only as instruction to the model; no code in writes/write_policy/summary inspects, flags, or refuses an incrementality claim. The one code occurrence is a hardcoded demo string a test asserts exists. On the live path compliance is voluntary and erodes with context/drift.
findings.recommendation: Emit a machine-inserted 'platform-attributed, not incremental' qualifier on every ROAS/CPA figure independent of the LLM; add an offline eval that fails when an answer labels attributed performance as incremental.
findings.failure_scenario: In a long session the model presents attributed ROAS as incremental return and recommends scaling spend on that basis, with nothing in code to catch it.

findings.title: Below break-even equates break-even with ROAS 1.0 (margin-blind)
evidence: platform/packages/core/src/audit/packs/core-performance.ts:76-99 (roas<1 titled below break-even; no margin input)
findings.description: True break-even ROAS is 1/contribution-margin (2.5x at 40% margin). Hardcoding break-even at 1.0 treats revenue as 100% profit, catching only campaigns losing money on gross revenue and missing the band above 1.0 but below margin-adjusted break-even. The only profit-sounding concept in the codebase gives false reassurance.
findings.recommendation: Rename to 'ROAS below 1.0 (revenue < spend)' until a margin profile exists; then make the threshold 1/margin per store/product line and label the input source.
findings.failure_scenario: A campaign at 1.8x ROAS on a 40% margin store is losing money but is never flagged; a merchant trusting the label keeps spending.

findings.title: Cross-platform total ignores timezone mismatch; TIMEZONE_MISMATCH never set
evidence: engine/src/paid_media_agent/tools/compute.py:152-154 (rejects mixed tz within a platform read)
engine/src/paid_media_agent/tools/compute.py:316-326 (cross-platform gate checks currency/completeness/metric/window dates, not timezone)
findings.description: Two platforms with the same date label but different timezones (Riyadh vs LA, up to 11h) are combined; late-day conversions move across the window boundary and the blended total treats them as the same day. A13 probe combined America/Los_Angeles and Asia/Riyadh with all quality flags [].
findings.recommendation: Set TIMEZONE_MISMATCH when platform timezones differ and either suppress the total or state it in total_suppressed_reason/notes.
findings.failure_scenario: A blended daily total for a Riyadh and an LA account double-books or drops conversions near the day boundary, misstating a day-over-day move.

findings.title: Pacing uses active-day denominator; over_budget can mislabel under-delivery
findings.description: average_daily divides spend by days-with-rows, not window days; a campaign that spent on 2 of 14 days has its average inflated and can appear over_budget while actually under-delivering across the window. The field label implies window-day averaging; the code uses active-day averaging.
findings.recommendation: Report both active-day and window-day averages; base over_budget on window coverage; or rename the field to match the math.
findings.failure_scenario: A sparse-delivery campaign under-pacing over the period is flagged over_budget on its active-day average; the operator cuts a budget that was actually under-delivering.

findings.title: ATTRIBUTION_DIFFERS and four other quality flags are declared but never produced; attribution metadata is dropped
evidence: engine/src/paid_media_agent/tools/direct/x_ads.py:367 and openai_ads.py:257 (attribution at payload top level)
findings.description: Five of ten quality flags have zero producers; the taxonomy overstates implemented coverage. Direct adapters even emit their attribution model as a top-level payload key, but reads.py normalizes only payload['rows'] so it is discarded before reaching source_fields. ATTRIBUTION_DIFFERS, the hook for the cross-platform attribution caveat, is inert.
findings.recommendation: Implement producers for each declared flag or remove the unused ones; persist attribution into artifact metadata and ReadResult and use it to populate ATTRIBUTION_DIFFERS; this is the prerequisite for DA-01's gate.
findings.failure_scenario: Readers of the enum and docs believe the system detects attribution/currency/timezone divergence; it detects none of them.

findings.title: No LTV / CAC / payback / cohort / store-verified revenue / MER (T5 missing)
evidence: platform/packages/core/src/model.ts:1-12 and engine/src/paid_media_agent/domain/metrics.py:49-67 (closed metric sets, only conversion_value)
docs/TODO.md:14-16 (store revenue does not exist yet)
findings.description: The only value is platform-attributed conversion_value; there is no customer identity, order/refund/COGS/margin source, CAC, payback, cohort or MER anywhere in either tree. CPA is cost-per-attributed-conversion, not CAC. Break-even and profit claims have no data to stand on. Honestly scoped as absent in docs.
findings.recommendation: Build read-only store/CRM connectors (Salla/Zid/Shopify), a structured company-context entity (margin, allowable CAC, payback), and a deterministic profit/MER/CAC compute beside compute.py with trust-tier labelling; keep platform-attributed ROAS side by side, never conflated.
findings.failure_scenario: A merchant asks whether spend is profitable; the only answer available is platform-attributed ROAS, which can diverge sharply from true contribution profit.

findings.title: No forecasting / trend / seasonality / Ramadan-Eid / locale-week awareness
evidence: exhaustive grep: forecast/predict/holt/arima/ewma/moving_average/rolling = 0 code hits; ramadan/eid/holiday/seasonal = prose only
findings.description: No statistical or ML forecasting, trend-detection, baseline, moving-average, regression, or seasonality code exists; comparison is a two-window equal-length delta only, on fixed rolling UTC blocks. Notable for an Arabic-first MENA product with no Ramadan/Eid/Hijri/weekend-locale handling. No doc claims these, so GAPs not defects.
findings.recommendation: If added, implement as deterministic tools (point estimate + interval, pacing-to-period-end) so numbers stay code-derived; add a Gregorian+Hijri holiday calendar and configurable weekend days per account/geo, plus YoY/Ramadan-aligned window selection.
findings.failure_scenario: The product cannot answer what spend/CPA will be next month, cannot pace to month-end, and has no structural awareness of Ramadan, the dominant MENA seasonal effect.

key_findings: Live data enters at trust tier T1 (raw, completeness unknown) but is rendered with T3/T4 confidence: every gate that should hold it back (data_complete_through completeness, provider reconciliation, attribution compatibility) is fixture-only or tautological on the live path.
reconciled=yes is tautological for live data (self-check vs self-check) AND the report hardcodes reconciled:true regardless of the body (DA-04/DA-05) - found independently by B1, B8, A13.

The cross-platform total sums conversions across incompatible attribution models and derives a blended CPA/ROAS with no attribution or timezone gate; ATTRIBUTION_DIFFERS and 4 other quality flags are declared but never produced (DA-01/DA-02/DA-20).

The AI can recommend on insufficient data at 10 concrete code locations; the key enabler is propose_change carrying no evidence artifact, no sample size, and blank-able measurement/reversal plans, with classify_risk blind to data basis (DA-11).

Ratios silently blend full spend with partial conversions/impressions and emit precise-looking but wrong CPA/CTR with no suppression (DA-06/DA-07, VERIFIED_RUNTIME); small-base noise (2->3 conversions) is emitted as a structured anomaly flag (DA-10).

The money-write path turns data defects into financial risk: a zero-decimal currency produces a 100x budget (P1, DA-15), the overview sums across currencies with a structurally-0x ROAS tile (DA-12), and the percentage cap is bypassed when the prior budget is unknown with a null default absolute cap (DA-16).
Synthetic/demo data runs the production PolicyEngine/audit path with no per-row synthetic marker, gated only by a deploy-wide flag (DA-14) - demo code reaching a production path.
T5 business-verified truth (store revenue, COGS, margin, MER, CAC, LTV) is entirely MISSING; all 15 lead spot-checks of the specialists' citations held exactly.
B9.disagreements: The code contradicts its own docs in several load-bearing places, all re-verified: reports.py/render.py advertise a reconciled report while reconciled is hardcoded true and tautological for live data (DA-04/05); compare_periods.py:140 promises a cross-platform total only when sources are compatible, but compatibility never checks attribution or timezone (DA-01/20); metrics-and-attribution.md forbids adding conversion counts as deduplicated people yet compute.py:278-298 adds them into the rendered scorecard (DA-01); reporting-semantics.md:13,15 (missing stays absent; never sum across currencies) is violated by six providers coercing missing->0 (DA-18) and by live-data.tsx:33-41 summing across currencies (DA-12); the wiki tells the model that 'last N days' ends at data_complete_through, which no live path ever sets (DA-03); common.py presents a 10-flag taxonomy of which 5 are never produced (DA-02); instructions.md lists 'confidence' as something the agent explains but no confidence computation exists. Honest, non-contradicted gaps: forecasting, LTV/CAC/store-revenue and incrementality are scoped as absent in docs/TODO.md and customization.md - no public overclaim found. Inherited doc-hygiene note from A13: the brief's engine/domain/metrics.py path is actually engine/src/paid_media_agent/domain/metrics.py.
B9.not_verified: Live Pipeboard MCP payload shape - whether it could carry data_complete_through/totals/currency/attribution that the host currently ignores (needs a live allowlisted account; prohibited); all live-vs-fixture conclusions are VERIFIED_CODE on the host side but INFERRED on the wire. Live-LLM behavior under thin/noisy data and whether it honors the prose confidence/incrementality guardrails at inference (no model API exercised; scripted/offline path only). Runtime behavior of the Next.js dashboard tiles against live/sandbox providers (static call chain only; DA-12 argued statically). Real provider minor-unit behavior for zero/3-decimal currencies against live APIs (DA-15 from Meta docs + code). Whether the X Ads/OpenAI Ads direct adapters and MARKTING_DEMO_MODE are reachable in a shipped production configuration or gated behind settings (affects the production blast radius of DA-03 and DA-14). End-to-end runtime of the cross-engine float-vs-Decimal divergence at scale (DA-09 is VERIFIED_CODE, not measured).

A16.scope: Consolidated specialist reports A1-A15; produced executive gap analysis (01-media-buying-gap-analysis.md) and channel x capability matrix (09-media-buyer-capability-matrix.md); re-verified 17 citations against source code.
tests_executed: read-only spot-check reads only (sed/grep) => exit 0
no test suites re-run by A16 (specialists executed theirs); consolidation is read-only

findings.title: Zero-decimal currency (JPY/KRW...) produces a 100x budget
evidence: CENTS_TO_MICROS=10_000 / UNITS_TO_MICROS two-decimal assumption hard-coded in budget unit conversion
findings.description: Budget writes assume every currency has 2 decimal places. For zero-decimal currencies a budget can be scaled 100x. VERIFIED_CODE; runtime NOT_VERIFIED (no live platform).
findings.recommendation: Derive minor-unit scaling from the account currency (ISO 4217 exponent) instead of a constant; add a test for JPY/KRW.

findings.title: Typed Meta status/budget writes never verify the object belongs to account_id
findings.description: Typed Meta write tools skip the ownership check the generic tools do, so a caller could act on an object not in the enabled account scope (policy + account-scope bypass).
findings.recommendation: Apply the same assertOwnedResource/account-scope check to every typed write, not just generic api_update.

findings.title: protected_accounts policy bypassable for Google by reformatting the customer id
findings.description: The protected-accounts guard matches on a customer id string; reformatting (dashes/customers prefix) evades it for Google.
findings.recommendation: Normalize customer ids to a canonical form before every policy comparison.

findings.title: Workspace account-scope bypass via single-resource/raw reads (Reddit, TikTok, Microsoft)
findings.description: Reddit single-resource read paths, TikTok reads forcing only advertiser_id (not advertiser_ids/bc_id), and Microsoft customer-management reads let a member enumerate or read entities outside the tenant's enabled-account set.
findings.recommendation: Enforce the enabled-account set on every read path, including single-resource and customer-management endpoints.

findings.title: apple_upload_asset is an arbitrary server-file read + SHA-256 oracle in the multi-tenant runtime
findings.description: The Apple asset-upload tool reads a server-side file path and returns a hash, usable as a file-read/existence oracle in the shared cloud runtime.
findings.recommendation: Restrict to tenant-scoped uploaded blobs; never accept arbitrary server paths.

findings.title: Generic tiktok_api_update reaches permanent deletion
findings.description: TikTok deletes via */status/update + DELETE; DELETE is excluded from the typed enum but reachable through the generic update tool, enabling irreversible data loss within a tenant.
findings.recommendation: Block DELETE/permanent-status transitions in the generic update guard.

findings.title: Cross-platform blended ROAS/CPA sums non-comparable attribution and windows
findings.description: The engine sums conversions and conversion_value across platforms with different conversion definitions and attribution windows and emits one blended CPA/ROAS; the attribution-mismatch flag is never set. Unsafe as a decision input.
findings.recommendation: Stamp rows with window + conversion definition; refuse to total across incompatible definitions, mirroring the existing mixed-currency suppression.

findings.title: Conversions coerced to 0 (not null); zero-conversion/negative-roas rules auto-propose pausing healthy campaigns
findings.description: Providers emit 0 for absent conversions/value; the zero-conversion-spend and negative-roas rules then flag and recommend pausing campaigns whose objective is not purchase (e.g. awareness, lead-gen), contradicting the semantics doc.
findings.recommendation: Emit null for missing metrics; make rules objective-aware and skip rows with unknown conversion data.

findings.title: Budget policy evaluated at validate time only; apply re-plans against fresh state
findings.description: Only protected-accounts is re-checked at apply(); budget caps are not re-evaluated, so a value changing between validate and apply can exceed the cap.
findings.recommendation: Re-run checkBudgetPolicy at apply() against the re-fetched current value.

findings.title: Absolute budget cap is currency-blind; pct cap bypassed when prior budget unknown; default has no absolute ceiling
evidence: platform/packages/core/src/policy/engine.ts:140-151 (pct branch guarded by fromMicros>0; absCap nullable)
findings.description: The absolute cap compares raw micros across currencies; the percentage-delta cap is silently skipped when fromMicros is unknown/zero; default policy sets no absolute ceiling.
findings.recommendation: Make the absolute cap currency-aware; treat unknown prior budget as a hard stop, not a bypass; ship a sane default ceiling.

findings.title: Cloud overview ROAS tile is structurally 0x; overview totals sum across currencies
findings.description: The dashboard summary requests metrics without conversion_value, so the blended ROAS tile computes to 0x; spend/value tiles also sum across mixed currencies.
findings.recommendation: Request conversion_value; compute per-currency and label; do not sum across currencies.

findings.title: AI engine cannot read six of eleven channels (TikTok, Snap, Microsoft, Pinterest, Spotify, Apple)
findings.description: The engine normalizes only six platforms; six channels have no fixture, no normalization, and several no write bridge, so the 'AI media buyer' cannot reason about them offline and only stores raw payloads live.
findings.recommendation: Add fixtures, normalization and bridge mappings for all shipped channels, or stop advertising them as managed.

findings.title: Reporting silently truncated then labelled complete
findings.description: Google GAQL returns up to 10k rows, TikTok fetches only page 1, Microsoft ignores limit; results are presented as complete and truncated is never set, so a buyer silently reasons on a partial dataset.
findings.recommendation: Paginate or set truncated=true and surface completeness.

findings.title: No attribution-window transparency; windows hidden/mixed; timezone mismatch ignored
findings.description: ReportRow/PerformanceRow carry no attribution field; windows are fixed or account-default and never surfaced; cross-platform totals ignore timezone mismatch.
findings.recommendation: Add attribution + timezone metadata to every row and to the UI.

findings.title: Several channels create non-servable campaigns
evidence: A2-06 platform/packages/google/src/tools.ts:41 (enum accepts PMax/Shopping/Video, builds Search); A4-08; A7; A8
findings.description: Google accepts PMax/Shopping/Video channel types but builds a Search-shaped campaign; Snap/Pinterest/X/Microsoft create shells with unvalidated objective and no children, so created campaigns cannot deliver.
findings.recommendation: Validate objective/type and either build the real shape or reject.

findings.title: Derived ratios return 0 (not null) on zero denominators
findings.description: CPA/CPC/CPM and ROAS are emitted as 0 when denominators are zero, misreporting 'free' performance or ROAS-unavailable as 0, contradicting the no-fabricated-zeroes doctrine.
findings.recommendation: Emit null for undefined ratios.

findings.title: Per-provider conversion definitions differ and the UI never says which
findings.description: 'conversions' means purchase (Meta/Snap/Reddit/Spotify), checkout (Pinterest), install (Apple), website-conversion (LinkedIn), or account-defined (Google/MS/TikTok), with no indication to the user; lead-gen leads are invisible.
findings.recommendation: Carry and display the conversion definition per row; capture leads where applicable.

findings.title: No rate-limit retry/backoff; token refresh on every runtime assembly
findings.description: Several providers have no 429/backoff handling and refresh OAuth tokens on every request assembly, risking throttling and refresh races in the cloud.
findings.recommendation: Add backoff on rate-limit codes and cache/rotate tokens safely.

findings.title: Docs contradict code (doctor adapter topology, Apple API version, always-paused, Snap claims)
findings.description: doctor says LinkedIn is a direct adapter though it routes via Pipeboard; Apple docs say v5 while code is v1; 'always paused' is delivered by policy not code; Snap docs overstate capability.
findings.recommendation: Reconcile docs with code; treat tool descriptions as contracts.

findings.title: Gated providers off by default when .env.example is copied
findings.description: LinkedIn, Pinterest, Spotify and the TikTok rollout gate are disabled for every org under the shipped example config, so connectors appear present but inert.
findings.recommendation: Document the enable switches prominently or default-enable vetted providers.

findings.title: GAP: no business economics (store revenue, profit, MER, CAC, LTV, contribution margin)
evidence: A12-08; docs/TODO.md section 3 ('Nothing exists yet ... ROAS uses platform-attributed conversion value')
findings.description: The product optimizes platform-reported conversion value, not the business's money. No store/CRM revenue, orders, refunds, COGS, margin, CAC, MER or LTV exist anywhere. This is the largest gap for an 'AI media buyer'.
findings.recommendation: Build the read-only store/CRM revenue layer the TODO already plans and join it to spend for MER/CAC/profit.

findings.title: GAP: no creative intelligence (inventory, fatigue, winners, clusters, lifecycle, testing)
evidence: A14-01 (no creative entity in core model or engine domain/metrics.py:49); A14-03 (prompts reference a get_creative_performance tool the catalog lacks)
findings.description: No creative entity/attribute/table exists; no fatigue (no reach/frequency), no winner detection below campaign grain, no clusters/lifecycle/testing; prompts hallucinate creative tooling.
findings.recommendation: Add a creative subsystem (entity, ad-level performance with frequency, fatigue, significance) and remove ungrounded prompt claims.

findings.title: GAP: no forecasting, scaling, cross-channel allocation, or learning loop

findings.description: Decision intelligence (marginal ROAS, diminishing returns, budget sizing, allocation, forecasting) and memory (recommendation/outcome tracking) are absent; the system does not learn from what it recommended or what happened.

key_findings: No cell in the channel x capability matrix is FULL: reporting peaks at READ_ONLY and the campaign-level write surface is safe but narrow; everything a buyer calls analysis or economics is PARTIAL or MISSING across all 11 channels.

Largest strategic gap is economics: no store revenue, profit, MER, CAC, LTV or contribution margin anywhere (F-21); the product optimizes platform-attributed conversion value, which docs/TODO.md itself admits is not real revenue.
The AI engine can only reason about 5 of 11 channels (Meta, Google, Reddit, LinkedIn, X); TikTok/Snap/Microsoft/Pinterest/Spotify/Apple have no engine data path (F-12).

Five P0 safety defects: 100x zero-decimal currency budget, Meta typed-write ownership bypass, Google protected-account bypass, a cluster of workspace-scope read bypasses, and an Apple arbitrary-file-read oracle.

Attribution is unsafe when blended: the engine sums non-comparable conversions/windows into one ROAS/CPA with the mismatch flag never set (F-07), and conversion zero-coercion can auto-propose pausing healthy campaigns (F-08).
The cloud overview ROAS tile is structurally 0x because conversion_value is never requested, and totals sum across currencies (F-11).

Safety machinery (two-step validate->apply gate, hash-bound pending ops, protected accounts, account scoping, forced-paused creation, append-only audit) is genuinely strong and consistently applied across all providers.
Specialist corpus is high quality: 17/17 spot-checked citations confirmed on substance; only blemish was A4 Snapchat's stale line numbers (file is 172 lines; substance verified at provider.ts:139).
